facts.text: When the railroad bypassed the town in 1899, Jacob Bartles moved his store north, founding what would become Bartlesville.
In 1905, oil pioneer Frank Phillips founded Phillips Petroleum in Bartlesville, turning the city into the birthplace of a global energy giant.
Frank Lloyd Wright’s only fully realized skyscraper, the Price Tower, crowns Bartlesville’s skyline and earned National Historic Landmark status.
Bartlesville was the test site for America’s first pay‑cable television experiment in 1957, airing The Pajama Game to 300 homes.
The annual OKM Music Festival, formerly OK Mozart, brings world‑renowned musicians like Itzhak Perlman and Joshua Bell to Bartlesville each summer.
Bartlesville’s streetcar system, begun in 1908, marked the town’s early commitment to public transportation.
